name: OXACOR-300 TAB (BL) 10*10
description: Oxacor-300 Tablet is a medication used to treat and prevent seizures, but cannot cure epilepsy. It can be taken alone or in combination with other medications, with the dose and frequency determined by the doctor. It can be taken with or without food, and it usually takes a couple of weeks to work. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, dizziness, fatigue, and low sodium levels. Long-term treatment can cause osteoporosis and increase the risk of bone fractures. Anticonvulsants like Oxacor 300 may also cause suicidal thoughts. It is important to inform your doctor about any medical conditions, including heart problems, kidney or liver disease, difficulty urinating, depression, or suicidal thoughts. Pregnant women should consult their doctor before starting or stopping the medication.

name: DEAXAT TAB (BL) 10*10
description: DEAXAT TABLET is a combination of two medications used to treat depression by increasing chemical messengers in the brain. It can be taken with or without food, and should be taken at the same time each day. Common side effects include dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision, increased heart rate, muscle rigidity, restlessness, and tremor. It may cause sudden blood pressure drops, dizziness, sleepiness, and weight gain. Before taking it, consult a doctor if you have any medical conditions.

name: MYCOLATE-500 TAB (ALU) 10*1*10
description: Mycolate-500 Tablet is an immunosuppressant medication used to prevent organ rejection after transplants by suppressing the body’s immune system. It is taken on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal, and should be taken regularly. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, headache, high blood pressure, and changes in white blood cell count. It may increase the risk of infections and certain cancers. It is not recommended for pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding individuals. It is important to inform your doctor about any signs of infection or unexpected bleeding and inform your healthcare team about any other medications that may affect this medication.

name: UDICAD-300 TAB (BL-MONO) 10*1*15
description: Udicad-300 Tablet is a medication used to dissolve gallstones and treat primary biliary cirrhosis. It breaks down cholesterol in the gallbladder, preventing their formation. The dosage depends on the condition and body weight. Common side effects include abdominal pain, diarrhea, hair loss, itching, nausea, and rash. Patients should inform their doctor if they experience gallbladder inflammation, frequent cramps, blood coughing, or rapid weight gain. Udicad may also require ultrasound scans or blood tests to monitor liver function.

name: TESTONOL-40 CAP (BL) 10*1*10
description: Testonol 40 capsule is a medication used to treat male hypogonadism caused by low testosterone levels. It is prescribed to men with known medical conditions and is injected directly into the skin or muscles under doctor’s supervision. Common side effects include edema, swelling, weight gain, coughing, vomiting, increased erection, and injection site reactions. It is important to inform your doctor about any history of high blood pressure, heart attack, stroke, and other medications, as these may affect its effectiveness. Regular blood tests may be performed to monitor testosterone and prostate-specific antigen levels.

name: HI-CROST INJ 5ML  (WFI-MONO)

description: Estranol Tablet is a hormone replacement therapy (HRT) used to treat symptoms of menopause, estrogen deficiency, and osteoporosis. Side effects include headaches, breast pain, irregular vaginal bleeding, abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, and hair loss. Warning signs include breast lumps, unusual vaginal bleeding, dizziness, faintness, severe headaches, chest pain, shortness of breath, and leg pains. Before taking this medication, consult a doctor if you have a history of these symptoms, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or have any medical conditions.

name: DYDRONOL TAB (MONO-BL) 10*1*10
description: Dydronol 10mg Tablet is a hormone replacement therapy used to treat conditions caused by progesterone deficiencies, including female infertility, menstrual pain, PMS, endometriosis, abnormal uterine bleeding, and miscarriage. It is prescribed by a doctor and should be taken daily, preferably whole with water. Side effects include headache, nausea, vaginal bleeding, breast pain, and bleeding or spotting between menstrual periods. Patients should discuss any previous medical history, regular medications, and pregnancy or breastfeeding with their doctor before starting treatment.

name: CLOMIFAN-50 TAB (BL) 10*5*10
description: Clomifan-50 Tablet is a medication used to treat female infertility, affecting women with ovulation problems or PCOS. It should be taken daily, with or without food, and is not safe for long-term use. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, bloating, headache, and hot flushes. It is important to inform your doctor about any history of early menopause, infertility, ovarian fibroids, or swollen ovary, and any other medications you are taking. Avoid alcohol while taking Tablet.

name: OMEZOSE-20 CAP (STRIP) 20*20
description: Omezose-20 Capsule is a medication used to reduce stomach acid production and treat acid-related stomach and intestine diseases like heartburn, acid reflux, peptic ulcer disease, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. Long-term use may increase the risk of bone fractures. Before taking Capsule, inform your doctor about any liver problems, allergies, or bone loss. name: NOLL-TZ TAB (BL) 20*10

Pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult a doctor before taking this medication.

name: MESANOL-1200 TAB (BL-MONO) 10*1*15

Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, headache, itching, flatulence, and vomiting. If symptoms persist or worsen, contact a doctor. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor about any kidney or liver problems, stomach blockage, age, pregnancy, breastfeeding, and other medications.

name: ESONOL FAST-40 TAB (ALU) 10*10

The dosage depends on the condition and should be taken on an empty stomach, preferably in the morning or at least 1 hour before meal. It is important to avoid foods that worsen symptoms and reduce alcohol consumption. The medicine should be used regularly, at the same time each day, and should not be used if you have asthma, severe COPD, heart conditions, diabetes, breathing problems, thyroid or liver issues, or are pregnant or breastfeeding.
